children: and Turkish Airlines finalized an order for as many as 150 737 Max aircraft, completing discussions that began last year as the carrier expands its fleet and Istanbul-based network.

Turkish Airlines placed firm orders for 100 737-8 aircraft and took options for another 50 737 Max jets, Boeing said Wednesday. The agreement includes substitution rights allowing the airline to switch some aircraft to the larger 737-10.
The deal represents Turkish Airlines' largest Boeing
single-aisle order and adds to a major widebody commitment made last year. In 2025, the airline ordered as many as 75 Boeing 787 Dreamliners as part of its fleet expansion program.

with another sizable order for its 737 Max program while strengthening its position with one of the world's largest international carriers. Turkish Airlines and its AJet subsidiary currently operate more than 200 Boeing aircraft, including 737 Max, 737 Next-Generation, 777 and 787 models as well as 777 freighters.

Turkish Airlines has been expanding its fleet as it seeks to increase capacity across its domestic and international network. The carrier currently has 567 passenger and cargo aircraft serving 358 destinations in 133 countries.
The 737-8 aircraft are expected to be deployed on domestic and international routes. Boeing
said the Max family uses about 20% less fuel than the aircraft it replaces.
The agreement also includes industrial participation in Türkiye's aviation sector, although Boeing
didn't disclose financial terms or provide details about the scope of that work.
The order was finalized in the presence of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. Boeing
and Turkish Airlines had been discussing the aircraft purchase since 2025.
